findings.claim: No test sets the new prose-rule arm against a partner that carries rows and that the answer does NOT name. If namesThePartner is weakened to 'any row id matches' (the matchesText conjunct dropped), every finding-partner test still passes.
findings.evidence: Mutated `if (ids.contains(row.getId()) && namesAnyOf(lower, row))` to `if (ids.contains(row.getId()))`, then ran CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest, FindingPartnerLogDisclosureTest, LlmInferenceServiceAnswerFromFindingsContextTest, SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest and SubstanceInSeveralActiveOrdersTest (every test class outside ArchitectureGuardTest/DrugReferenceTestSupport that references findingPartners or the completion sentence). Result: 67 run, 0 failures. Under that mutation every interaction-rule partner is 'stated' whatever the prose says, so ADR Decision 100's appended sentence never fires for interaction findings. Why it survives: each pre-existing negative completion case goes through CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest.service(chart, chips, ...) at line 621, which builds DrugReferenceTestSupport.validatorRaising(null, chips). With no dataset, namesThePartner returns false early, so the arm is off in every negative case. All four new OverShippedData cases are positive. The #477 residue case's row-carrying finding (Metronidazole) is stated by containment anyway. Suggested case: the alprazolam arrangement, answer citing both findings but naming only Nevirapine, expecting the 'not named above: active order Rifampicin (rifampin)' sentence and {named 2, stated 1}. Tree restored with git checkout.

verdict: Mergeable: it fixes #555 (with the prose arm switched off, the four new cases reproduce the ticket's exact appended sentence, and with it on they pass) by the codebase's established approach (rows carried structurally plus matchesText, as namesTheEndedOrderDrug and namesTheFindingsSubject already do). The main remaining gap is that nothing pins the new arm in the negative direction.
what_i_swept: Read SKILL.md, the PR body, issue #555 and both nested CLAUDE.md files (reference rules on matching a drug name, #151 two-resolutions, #172 getAll memo, #439 logging). Confirmed git diff main...HEAD --stat = 15 files +493/-69. Read the full production diff and the test diff. Traced outward. (1) Partner-row keys: partnerName/chipPartnerName equal namedPartners at both arms, collapseSharedMechanisms unions by the same key, and partnerRowIds re-keys by namedPartners(). (2) Every SafetyWarning copy path forwards partnerRows (withEndedOrder, withMatchedOrderNames, currentOrderDisplays, statedInTheAnswer, subjectRows). (3) RecordMapping: grepped for copy sites that would drop the new stamp and found none, so the constructor pads/cuts to the findingPartners size. (4) Interaction chips with no rows: question-pair arm (3-arg constructor, no namedPartners), class-only, #477 factories, condition-mediated. All are documented. (5) rowsOfSubstance inputs match what chartOrderBridges computes in both arms. (6) getAll() is reached only when rows exist, i.e. after the dataset loaded, so the un-try'd withUnstatedPartnersNamed path does not gain a throw on a disabled install. (7) Precedent: namesTheEndedOrderDrug (#478 round 2) and namesTheFindingsSubject (#515) use the same lowercase + namesAnyOf and id-to-getAll shapes. (8) Docs: ADR Decision 100's body, README:555, the ChartSearchService and FindingPartnerCoverageCheck javadoc and the InteractionClaimPairFidelityCheck sentence: no surviving claim that containment is the only test. Ran at head: CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest + FindingPartner*Test + InteractionClaimPairFidelityTest + SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest (89 run, 0 failures), and ArchitectureGuardTest + ProjectInstructionsGuardTest (39 run, 0 failures). Mutations: (a) namesThePartner forced false: 4 of the new cases redden with exactly the ticket's sentence, which confirms the fix resolves the repro. (b) The matchesText conjunct dropped: all 67 tests in the five finding-partner suites stay green (F1). Approach alternatives weighed: stripping the label's parenthetical, which ADR/CLAUDE.md forbid as a fourth name matcher; and matching against findingBridgeNames (order displays), which are not partner-aligned on a merged finding. The PR's choice is better than either.
